from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the three displayed derived Hom objects: generic dg-quotient infrastructure through the recorded ancestry, specifically the finite-cone argument in the final step of lem-coef-dg-quotient-hom-cone. The triangulated structure is obtained from a general cone-closed module-category criterion, before proving invariance of the finite hull. Abstract dg-category axioms (A), (B), (C) supply the generic triangulation theorem used after the module and sign checks. Technical input: Simultaneous admissible replacement of a finite dg diagram.

title: Simultaneous admissible replacement of a finite dg diagram
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a small cochain dg category over $\mathbf Z$ (a set of objects, cochain complexes of abelian groups $\mathcal A(x,y)$ as morphism objects, and associative unital compositions $\mathcal A(y,z)\otimes\mathcal A(x,y)\to\mathcal A(x,z)$ which are chain maps, so that $\partial(gh)=(\partial g)h+(-1)^{|g|}g\partial h$ for homogeneous $g,h$), with Hom differential $\partial$. Write $Z^0\mathcal A$ for closed degree-zero maps and $H^0\mathcal A$ for their classes modulo degree-minus-one boundaries. Assume (A) a zero object and dg binary sums, whose inclusions and projections are closed degree-zero maps satisfying the biproduct identities. Assume (B) dg functors $[n]$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, with $[0]=1$, $[n+m]=[n][m]$, and composition-compatible cochain isomorphisms $\mathcal A(x,y[n])\cong\mathcal A(x,y)[n]$, where $V[n]^j=V^{j+n}$ and $d_{V[n]}=(-1)^nd_V$. A sequence $u\xrightarrow{a}v\xrightarrow{b}w$ in $Z^0\mathcal A$ is called admissible when there are graded degree-zero maps $\pi:v\to u$ and $s:w\to v$ such that $\pi a=1$, $bs=1$, $a\pi+sb=1$, $ba=0$, and $\pi s=0$; its boundary is the closed map $\delta=\pi\partial s:w\to u[1]$ under (B). A map is an admissible monomorphism if it is the first arrow of such a sequence. Assume (C) that each closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$ has an admissible sequence $y\xrightarrow{i_f}c(f)\xrightarrow{p_f}x[1]$ with boundary $f[1]$. A homotopy equivalence is a closed degree-zero map with a closed degree-zero inverse modulo boundaries. For each integer $N\geq1$ and sequence of closed degree-zero maps $x_1\xrightarrow{f_1}x_2\to\cdots\xrightarrow{f_{N-1}}x_N$, there are objects $y_i$, admissible monomorphisms $j_i:y_i\to y_{i+1}$, and homotopy equivalences $r_i:y_i\to x_i$, with $y_1=x_1$, $r_1=1$, and $r_{i+1}j_i=f_ir_i$ as strict closed maps for $1\leq i<N$.

proof.text: Use the dg Leibniz rule $\partial(vu)=(\partial v)u+(-1)^{|v|}v\partial u$, which is the chain-map composition condition in the cited definition. Under (B), write $\theta_x:x\to x[1]$ and $\eta_x:x[1]\to x$ for the mutually inverse closed graded maps of degrees $-1$ and $1$ corresponding to the identity under shifting. For a cone sequence $y\xrightarrow{a_f}C(f)\xrightarrow{b_f}x[1]$ choose the splitting $(\pi_f,s_f)$ specified by (C). Its boundary condition reads $\pi_f\partial s_f=f\eta_x$. Differentiating the five splitting identities gives $b_f\partial s_f=0$, $(\partial\pi_f)a_f=0$, and $(\partial\pi_f)s_f=-\pi_f\partial s_f$. Therefore $\partial s_f=(a_f\pi_f+s_fb_f)\partial s_f=a_ff\eta_x$ and $\partial\pi_f=(\partial\pi_f)(a_f\pi_f+s_fb_f)=-f\eta_xb_f$. These are direct consequences of the stated cone and dg axioms, not an invocation of a triangle theorem.

source.place: Tag 09P6, lemma-get-triangle, proof equations (1)-(6); Tag 09QJ, situation-ABC, boundary condition (C).

proof.text: For $f=1_x$, abbreviate its cone data by $C,a,b,\pi,t$. The degree-minus-one endomorphism $h=t\theta_x\pi$ satisfies $\partial h=(a\eta_x)\theta_x\pi-t\theta_x(-\eta_xb)=a\pi+tb=1_C$. Here the minus sign is the Leibniz sign for $t\theta_x$ of degree $-1$; $\eta_x\theta_x=1_x$ and $\theta_x\eta_x=1_{x[1]}$. This proves identity-cone contractibility directly in two equalities, with no new lemma node.

source.place: Tag 09QK, lemma-id-cone-null, complete contraction calculation, with the shift identifications written explicitly.

proof.text: Fix a closed degree-zero $\alpha:x\to y$. By (A) set $M=y\oplus C(1_x)$, with closed inclusions $I:y\to M$, $J:C(1_x)\to M$ and projections $P:M\to y$, $Q:M\to C(1_x)$. Put $j=I\alpha+Ja$ and $r=P$. These are closed degree-zero maps and $rj=\alpha$. The closed map $I$ obeys $rI=1_y$. By the preceding contraction, the degree-minus-one map $H=JhQ$ has $\partial H=JQ=1_M-IP$, since $J,Q$ are closed. Thus $r$ is a homotopy equivalence with inverse $I$. Admissibility of $j$ will be proved by exhibiting its quotient in the next two steps.

source.place: Tag 09QM, lemma-factor, direct-sum construction and final homotopy calculation; $h$ contracts $1_{C(1_x)}$, not $1_x$.

proof.text: Choose a cone sequence $y\xrightarrow{a'}D=C(\alpha)\xrightarrow{b'}x[1]$ with graded splitting $(\pi',t')$, by (C). Define the degree-zero map $q:M\to D$ by $q=a'(P-\alpha\pi Q)-t'bQ$. This quotient is the cone object $D$, not the dg direct sum $y\oplus x[1]$. By the identities of Step 1, $\partial\pi=-\eta_x b$ and $\partial t'=a'\alpha\eta_x$. Since $a',P,\alpha,Q,b$ are closed, $\partial q=a'\alpha\eta_x bQ-a'\alpha\eta_x bQ=0$. Also $qj=a'(\alpha-\alpha\pi a)-t'ba=0$. This checks the closedness and zero-composite conditions that a merely graded quotient would not provide.

source.place: Tag 09QM, lemma-factor, missing admissible-quotient verification repaired using a cone from Tag 09QJ, situation-ABC; differential identities from Tag 09P6, lemma-get-triangle.

proof.text: Set $\rho=\pi Q:M\to x$ and $\sigma=I\pi'-Jtb':D\to M$, graded degree-zero maps, with no assertion that they are closed. The splitting identities for $C(1_x)$ and $D$ give $\rho j=\pi a=1_x$ and $\rho\sigma=-\pi tb'=0$. They also give $q\sigma=a'\pi'+t'b'=1_D$. Expanding the other composite gives $\sigma q=I(P-\alpha\pi Q)+JtbQ$; hence $j\rho+\sigma q=IP+J(a\pi+tb)Q=IP+JQ=1_M$. Together with $qj=0$ from Step 4, these are exactly the five identities defining the admissible sequence $x\xrightarrow{j}M\xrightarrow{q}D$. Consequently the single-arrow construction has an admissible monomorphism $j$ and homotopy equivalence $r$ satisfying $rj=\alpha$ strictly.

source.place: Tag 09QM, lemma-factor: explicit verification of the omitted graded splitting, using the corrected quotient $C(\alpha)$.

proof.text: Induct on the number $N\geq1$ of objects. For $N=1$, put $y_1=x_1$ and $r_1=1_{x_1}$; there is no arrow condition. Suppose the replacement through $x_{N-1}$ has been constructed, with $y_1=x_1$, $r_1=1$, each $r_i$ a homotopy equivalence, each $j_i$ admissible, and $r_{i+1}j_i=f_ir_i$ for $i<N-1$. The composite $\alpha=f_{N-1}r_{N-1}:y_{N-1}\to x_N$ is closed of degree zero by the dg Leibniz rule. Apply Steps 2-5 to this composite, naming the resulting $M,j,r$ as $y_N,j_{N-1},r_N$. They give precisely $r_Nj_{N-1}=f_{N-1}r_{N-1}$ strictly. Retain all earlier data and equations. This proves the induction step, including $N=2$ from the base case, and all required clauses.
